english: In a triangle $ABC$, let $a,b,c$ denote the lengths of the sides opposite to the angles $A,B,C$, respectively. Suppose $\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}=\dfrac13$ and $\tan\dfrac{B}{2}\tan\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac13$. Then $\tan\dfrac{B-C}{2}$ is equal to
hindi: एक त्रिभुज $ABC$ में माना $a,b,c$ क्रमशः कोणों $A,B,C$ की सम्मुख भुजाओं की लम्बाइयाँ हैं। माना $\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}=\dfrac13$ तथा $\tan\dfrac{B}{2}\tan\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac13$ है। तब $\tan\dfrac{B-C}{2}$ बराबर है
solution: Let $x=\tan\dfrac B2,\ y=\tan\dfrac C2,\ z=\tan\dfrac A2$. Since $A+B+C=\pi$: $xy+yz+zx=1\Rightarrow z(x+y)=1-xy=\dfrac23$
solution_full: Write $x=\tan\dfrac B2$, $y=\tan\dfrac C2$, $z=\tan\dfrac A2$; all are positive since each half-angle lies in $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
Conditional identity: $A+B+C=\pi$ gives $\dfrac{B+C}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac A2$, so $\tan\dfrac{B+C}{2}=\cot\dfrac A2$, i.e. $\dfrac{x+y}{1-xy}=\dfrac1z$, equivalently $xy+yz+zx=1$.
Check: the data describe the triangle with $a:b:c=3:4:2$, for which $\tan\dfrac B2\tan\dfrac C2=\dfrac{s-a}{s}=\dfrac13$ and $\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}=\dfrac13$.
originality_note: New: tan(B/2), tan(C/2) and tan(A/2) are recovered as unknowns from the product condition, the identity xy + yz + zx = 1 and Napier's analogy written in half-angle tangents, a small 3-unknown system (way 5: tangent rule and conditional identity). Closest known: direct Napier's analogy exercises with A given, and 'tan(B/2)tan(C/2) = (s-a)/s' exercises. Different because: angle A is not given and has to be found from the system before the tangent rule gives the answer.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, side, angle and symbol is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated which side is opposite which angle; checked that a triangle with these data exists (sides 3 : 4 : 2). Changed: No change.
key_step: Combining the half-angle identity xy + yz + zx = 1 with Napier's analogy to solve for tan(A/2).
justification: Two standard results must be linked into a small system before either gives the answer; options exclude the slips (sqrt15/9 is tan(A/2) itself). Comparable to 2024-P1-Q3 (L3), above the one-formula ratio of 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).
